correctness.rationale: Direct neighborhood calculation proves the parity-twisted graph isomorphism for every bipartite base, including isolated vertices. The join and two polynomial square identities follow by exact face bijections. For paths, shifting selected indices by two gives the binomial counts; a radius-two domination characterization gives precisely boundary offsets 0–2 and internal gaps 3–5 for maximal 2-packings. Summing those intervals gives the rational generating function and all facet sizes, proving purity exactly at 1,2,3,6. Independent exhaustively enumerated small graphs agree; calculations are corroborative, not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The open-packing problem on bipartite prisms previously had a scalar extremal identity but not the complete family of feasible sets. Identifying the exact two-component conflict graph determines all cardinality counts, all irredundant configurations, and the coloring polynomial simultaneously; the ladder specialization gives exact count of facets at each size and a nonmonotone purity exception at six rungs. This is a structural classification of a natural graph product rather than arbitrary small-order arithmetic or a renamed scalar bound.
